blocks.prompt: 1 (i) How many arrangements of the letters of the following word, taken all together, can be made? CURRICULUM
blocks.explanation:
We arrange all the letters of a word; some letters repeat.
Plan: count the letters, count each repeated letter, then use the formula for objects not all different.
steps:
Given: the word CURRICULUM.
To find: the number of arrangements of all its letters.
Method: \(n\) objects of which \(n_1\) are alike, \(n_2\) are alike, ... can be arranged in \(\dfrac{n!}{n_1!\,n_2! \cdots}\) ways.

Count the letters
C, U, R, R, I, C, U, L, U, M
\[n = 10\]
\[\text{C} = 2,\ \text{U} = 3,\ \text{R} = 2\]
Why: I, L and M appear once each and need no division (1! = 1).

Apply the formula
\[\dfrac{10!}{2!\,3!\,2!} = \dfrac{3628800}{2 \cdot 6 \cdot 2}\]
\[= \dfrac{3628800}{24} = 151200\]
Why: Swapping the two C's, the three U's or the two R's among themselves gives the same word, so each word was counted 2! 3! 2! = 24 times.

Check the letter count
\[2 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 10 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The group sizes (C, U, R, I, L, M) must add up to the total number of letters.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) How many arrangements of the letters of the following word, taken all together, can be made? ADSORPTIVELY
blocks.explanation: Count the letters and look for repeats. Plan: if no letter repeats, the answer is simply \(n!\).
steps:
Given: the word ADSORPTIVELY.
To find: the number of arrangements of all its letters.
Method: \(n\) objects of which \(n_1\) are alike, \(n_2\) are alike, ... can be arranged in \(\dfrac{n!}{n_1!\,n_2! \cdots}\) ways.

Count the letters
A, D, S, O, R, P, T, I, V, E, L, Y
\[n = 12\]
Why: Checking letter by letter, no letter appears twice.

All letters different
\[12! = 479001600\]
Why: With no alike letters there is nothing to divide by; the arrangements are \({}^{12}P_{12} = 12!\).

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) How many arrangements of the letters of the following word, taken all together, can be made? PROBABILITY
blocks.explanation: Same type as (i). Plan: count letters, find repeats, apply the formula.
steps:
Given: the word PROBABILITY.
To find: the number of arrangements of all its letters.
Method: \(n\) objects of which \(n_1\) are alike, \(n_2\) are alike, ... can be arranged in \(\dfrac{n!}{n_1!\,n_2! \cdots}\) ways.

Count the letters
P, R, O, B, A, B, I, L, I, T, Y
\[n = 11\]
\[\text{B} = 2,\ \text{I} = 2\]
Why: All other letters appear once.

Apply the formula
\[\dfrac{11!}{2!\,2!} = \dfrac{39916800}{4}\]
\[= 9979200\]
Why: \(11! = 39916800\); the two B's and the two I's can each be swapped without making a new word.

Check the letter count
\[2 + 2 + 7 \times 1 = 11 \;\checkmark\]
Why: B, I and the seven single letters P, R, O, A, L, T, Y make 11.

blocks.text: The answer key prints a fourth answer, iv) 10810800, but Question 1 has only three words (i)-(iii). This entry matches no part of the question and should be ignored.
